question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo plumb-probe 1.0), then notifications/initialized, then tools/list, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.serverInfo: statsig-docs 1.1.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, capabilities tools.listChanged true; no mcp-session-id header is issued, and tools/list answers without one (section C and D of the artifact)
decoded.tools-served: five, in this order: get_page, list_pages, search_docs, amplitude_implementation_planner, send_docs_mcp_feedback. Every one carries execution.taskSupport "forbidden" and an optional rationale string of at most 500 characters, which the vendor's page describes as the model's explanation of why it called the tool
decoded.tools-documented: three. The vendor's Docs MCP server page, fetched 92 seconds later and byte-identical to the copy archived on 2026-09-17 (3001 bytes, SHA-256 b9a02b25...ad16), says under Available tools: "The server exposes three read-only tools", and lists get_page, list_pages and search_docs. It names neither of the other two anywhere (artifact section G)
decoded.the-two-undocumented-tools: amplitude_implementation_planner, described as assembling "an ordered multi-page setup sequence with code snippets for analytics, experiment, or session replay workflows", named for the parent company on a Statsig-branded server; and send_docs_mcp_feedback, described as "Report documentation gaps, broken examples, or ambiguous parameter descriptions to the Docs content backlog", taking a required category enum and a required message of up to 2000 characters
decoded.what-the-page-says-about-writing: the same page's Limitations note reads "The Docs MCP server is public, read-only, and serves English documentation only. It doesn't require authentication, doesn't expose MCP prompts or resources, and supports Streamable HTTP only", and its troubleshooting line reads "If you need project data or write access, this server isn't the right endpoint"
decoded.unchanged-since-2026-09-17: this reporter's own archive of 2026-09-17 carries the same tools/list response, tool for tool and description for description (pages.folded-2026-09-28.txt, section docs-mcp-tools-list.body.txt, 3160 bytes). The server did not change; version 5 of this entry recorded the page's number rather than the wire's
decoded.not-measured: no tool was called. send_docs_mcp_feedback was not exercised, because writing text into a vendor's content backlog unasked is not a read. Whether a call to it succeeds, and whether anything reaches any backlog, is unknown and is not claimed here

finding: With no credentials on 2026-09-29, tools/list on the public Statsig documentation MCP server returned five tools where the vendor's own page for that server says "The server exposes three read-only tools" and lists three. The two it does not name are amplitude_implementation_planner and send_docs_mcp_feedback, and the second takes a required message of up to 2000 characters which its description says is reported "to the Docs content backlog": a write path advertised to an unauthenticated caller by a server the same page calls read-only and directs elsewhere "if you need project data or write access". The page was fetched in the same pass and is byte-identical to the copy archived on 2026-09-17, and this reporter's 2026-09-17 transcript carries the same five tools, so neither side moved in twelve days. The tool was not called; what is measured is what the server advertises to a stranger.

reproducibility.command: H=https://docs.statsig.com;U=$H/api/mcp;A='content-type: application/json';B='accept: application/json, text/event-stream';curl -s -X POST $U -H "$A" -H "$B" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"plumb-probe","version":"1.0"}}}';curl -s -X POST $U -H "$A" -H "$B" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}';curl -s -X POST $U -H "$A" -H "$B" -H 'mcp-protocol-version: 2025-06-18' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}';curl -s $H/api/content/integrations/mcp/docs-mcp-server
